Detect Pairwise Interactions from a Mossy Forest Object

Source: R/detect_interaction.R
detect_interaction.Rd

Returns TreeSHAP pairwise interaction strengths for all stable features. Interaction values are computed during model fitting and stored in the object, either by the Python backend (TreeExplainer.shap_interaction_values()) or by the pure R backend with r_shap = "treeshap". They are not available with r_shap = "permutation" or when compute_interactions = FALSE.

Usage

detect_interaction(object, thresh = 0, all = FALSE, verbose = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

object

A mossy_forest object.

thresh

Interaction strength threshold. Only pairs whose mean \(|\phi_{jk}|\) exceeds thresh are returned (those above the threshold). Set to 0 to return all pairs.

all

If TRUE, return every off diagonal pair (upper triangle) regardless of thresh. Default FALSE.

verbose

If TRUE, print the table of above threshold pairs (or a message if none are found). Default TRUE.

...

Ignored.

Value

A data frame with columns FeatureA, FeatureB, and Interaction_Strength (mean absolute TreeSHAP interaction), sorted by interaction strength descending. Invisibly when all = TRUE.

Details

The \(p \times p\) interaction matrix stored in object$shap_obj$interaction_matrix is defined as: $$M_{jk} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\phi_{jk}(x_i)|$$ where \(\phi_{jk}(x_i)\) is the TreeSHAP interaction value for the pair \((j, k)\) at observation \(i\) (Lundberg et al., 2018). Diagonal entries are main effects and off diagonal entries are pairwise interactions.

References

Lundberg, S. M., Erion, G., Chen, H., DeGrave, A., Prutkin, J. M., Nair, B., Katz, R., Himmelfarb, J., Bansal, N., & Lee, S.-I. (2020). From local explanations to global understanding with explainable AI for trees. Nature Machine Intelligence, 2, 56-67.

Examples

# A small simulated regression problem with two modules of features
set.seed(1)
n <- 60
z <- rnorm(n)
X <- data.frame(a1 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), a2 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3),
                a3 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), b1 = rnorm(n), b2 = rnorm(n),
                b3 = rnorm(n))
y <- z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)
membership <- c(a1 = "A", a2 = "A", a3 = "A", b1 = "B", b2 = "B", b3 = "B")

# The pure R backend needs no Python installation
fit <- mf(X, y, module_membership = membership,
          screen_params = screen_control(min_ntree = 50),
          select_params = select_control(n_reps = 10, min_ntree = 50),
          final_ntree = 50, backend = "R", r_shap = "treeshap", verbose = 0, seed = 1)
detect_interaction(fit)
#>   FeatureA FeatureB Interaction_Strength
#> 1       a1       a2           0.06960101
